headline: S&P 500 Shiller CAPE Ratio Reaches Highest Level Since Dot-Com Bubble
summary: The S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio has reached its highest level since the dot-com bubble, according to market analysis.
why: The Shiller CAPE (Cyclically Adjusted Price-to-Earnings) ratio is a valuation metric that uses real earnings per share over a 10-year period to assess whether the broader stock market is overvalued or undervalued.

impacts.name: Broad US Equities
impacts.why: High valuation multiples can signal heightened risk of a market correction or lower long-term future equity returns.

why_moved: Elevated valuation metrics relative to historical norms prompt heightened caution among professional investors regarding potential equity market corrections.
